use: The illness or injury is the subject: kaze ga naoru.

example.ja: 風邪、もう治った？大丈夫？
example.english: Is your cold better? You okay?

examplePolite.romaji: kaze wa mou naorimashita ka? daijoubu desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 風邪はもう治りましたか？大丈夫ですか？
examplePolite.english: Has your cold cleared up? Are you all right?

notes: 直る naoru, same sound, is things getting fixed. Curing it yourself is naosu.

english: happen to see, spot, come across

example.romaji: kinou, eki de tanaka-san mikaketa yo.
example.ja: 昨日、駅で田中さん見かけたよ。
example.english: I saw Tanaka at the station yesterday.

examplePolite.romaji: kinou, eki de tanaka-san o mikakemashita yo.
examplePolite.ja: 昨日、駅で田中さんを見かけましたよ。
examplePolite.english: I happened to see Mr Tanaka at the station yesterday.

notes: Also for things you see around: saikin yoku mikakeru ne (you see those a lot lately).

example.ja: え、二人キスしたの？
example.english: Wait, you two kissed?

examplePolite.romaji: e, futari wa kisu shita n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: え、二人はキスしたんですか？
examplePolite.english: Wait, the two of you kissed?

notes: Casual and cute: chuu (suru).

example.ja: 一緒に踊ろうよ！
example.english: Come dance with me!

examplePolite.romaji: issho ni odorimasen ka?
examplePolite.ja: 一緒に踊りませんか？
examplePolite.english: Would you like to dance?

notes: dansu suru is also common, especially for modern dance.

example.ja: 昨日、階段で転んじゃった。
example.english: I tripped on the stairs yesterday.

examplePolite.romaji: kinou, kaidan de koronde shimaimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 昨日、階段で転んでしまいました。
examplePolite.english: I fell on the stairs yesterday.

notes: Collapsing or toppling over is taoreru.

use: You bump a thing into something: atama o butsukeru (bang your head).

example.ja: 痛い！棚に頭ぶつけた。
example.english: Ow! I banged my head on the shelf.

examplePolite.romaji: tana ni atama o butsukete shimaimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 棚に頭をぶつけてしまいました。
examplePolite.english: I banged my head on the shelf.

notes: butsukaru = to bump into (by itself): hito ni butsukaru.

use: You or a doctor does it: kaze o naosu.

example.ja: 早く風邪治してね。
example.english: Get over that cold soon.

examplePolite.romaji: hayaku kaze o naoshite kudasai ne.
examplePolite.ja: 早く風邪を治してくださいね。
examplePolite.english: I hope you get over your cold soon.

notes: 直す naosu, same sound, means fix or correct things.

use: futotta = I've put on weight; futotte iru = is fat.

example.ja: 最近ちょっと太っちゃったかも。
example.english: I might've put on a bit of weight lately.

examplePolite.romaji: saikin sukoshi futotte shimatta kamo shiremasen.
examplePolite.ja: 最近少し太ってしまったかもしれません。
examplePolite.english: I may have put on a little weight lately.

notes: Opposite: yaseru. Telling someone else futotta is rude.

use: yopparatteru = is drunk; yopparai = a drunk.

example.ja: 彼、もう酔っ払ってるよ。
example.english: He's already drunk.

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa mou yopparatte imasu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 彼はもう酔っ払っていますよ。
examplePolite.english: He's already drunk.

notes: A softer 'I'm a bit tipsy' is yotchatta.

use: Usually past: kaze hiita (I've got a cold).

example.ja: 喉痛い。風邪ひいたみたい。
example.english: My throat hurts. I think I've caught a cold.

examplePolite.romaji: nodo ga itai desu. kaze o hiita mitai desu.
examplePolite.ja: 喉が痛いです。風邪をひいたみたいです。
examplePolite.english: My throat hurts. I think I've caught a cold.

notes: Full form is kaze o hiku; don't swap in toru or motsu.

use: yaseta? (have you lost weight?) is a common compliment.

example.romaji: yaseta? nanka kirei ni natta ne.
example.ja: 痩せた？なんか綺麗になったね。
example.english: Have you lost weight? You look great.

examplePolite.romaji: yasemashita ka? kirei ni narimashita ne.
examplePolite.ja: 痩せましたか？綺麗になりましたね。
examplePolite.english: Have you lost weight? You look lovely.

notes: yasete iru = is thin. Opposite: futoru.

english: dry, get dry; get thirsty (nodo ga kawaku)

example.ja: 喉乾いた。なんか飲もう。
example.english: I'm thirsty. Let's get a drink.

examplePolite.romaji: nodo ga kawakimashita. nanika nomimashou.
examplePolite.ja: 喉が乾きました。何か飲みましょう。
examplePolite.english: I'm thirsty. Let's have something to drink.

notes: For thirst the strict kanji is 渇く. Laundry: sentakumono ga kawaita (the washing's dry).

example.ja: 雨でびしょびしょに濡れた。
example.english: I got soaked in the rain.

examplePolite.romaji: ame de bishobisho ni nuremashita.
examplePolite.ja: 雨でびしょびしょに濡れました。
examplePolite.english: I got soaked in the rain.

notes: Making something wet is nurasu.

english: turn on (a light, TV, AC); put on, attach
use: Switching on: denki o tsukeru. Opposite: kesu.

example.ja: もう暗いから、電気つけて。
example.english: It's getting dark, turn the light on.

examplePolite.romaji: kurai node, denki o tsukete kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 暗いので、電気をつけてください。
examplePolite.english: It's dark, so please turn on the light.

notes: ki o tsukete = take care. Also attach or apply: namae o tsukeru (give a name).

example.ja: これ、もう捨てていい？
example.english: Can I throw this out?

examplePolite.romaji: kore wa mou sutete mo ii desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: これはもう捨ててもいいですか？
examplePolite.english: Is it okay to throw this away?

notes: gomi o suteru = throw away rubbish. Also for dumping a person.

use: You open something; something opening by itself is aku.

example.ja: 暑いね。窓開けていい？
example.english: It's hot. Mind if I open the window?

examplePolite.romaji: atsui desu ne. mado o akete mo ii desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 暑いですね。窓を開けてもいいですか？
examplePolite.english: It's hot, isn't it. May I open the window?

notes: Opposite: shimeru (close).

english: cut; hang up (a phone); switch off

example.ja: あれ、髪切った？似合うね。
example.english: Oh, did you get a haircut? It suits you.

examplePolite.romaji: are, kami o kirimashita ka? niaimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: あれ、髪を切りましたか？似合いますね。
examplePolite.english: Oh, did you get your hair cut? It suits you.

notes: denwa o kiru = hang up. Not kiru 'wear' (着る): this one goes kirimasu, kitte; that one kimasu, kite.

use: Getting things ready, like food, drinks or documents.

example.romaji: nomimono wa watashi ga youi suru ne.
example.ja: 飲み物は私が用意するね。
example.english: I'll sort out the drinks.

examplePolite.romaji: nomimono wa watashi ga youi shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 飲み物は私が用意します。
examplePolite.english: I'll prepare the drinks.

notes: youi dekita? = ready? youi, don! = ready, set, go!

use: Waking someone else; waking up yourself is okiru.

example.ja: 明日7時に起こしてくれる？
example.english: Can you wake me at seven tomorrow?

examplePolite.romaji: ashita shichiji ni okoshite moraemasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 明日7時に起こしてもらえますか？
examplePolite.english: Could you wake me up at seven tomorrow?

notes: Also cause trouble: jiko o okosu (cause an accident).

use: Upper-body or whole-body clothes; trousers and shoes are haku, hats kaburu.

example.ja: 明日のパーティー、何着る？
example.english: What are you wearing to the party tomorrow?

examplePolite.romaji: ashita no paatii ni wa nani o kimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 明日のパーティーには何を着ますか？
examplePolite.english: What will you wear to the party tomorrow?

notes: kite iru = is wearing. Sounds like kiru 'cut', but goes kimasu, kite.
